newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: EU backs Israel visit, seeks Mideast peace drive.
newsitem.headline: EU backs Israel visit, seeks Mideast peace drive.

text.p: The European Union challenged Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday to turn his talks with PLO chairman Yasser Arafat this week into a breakthrough for the Middle East peace process.
"We hope the prospects of a breakthrough that this meeting raised will be delivered," Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring told a news conference at informal two-day talks between EU foreign ministers.

Spring said it was vital that a fact-finding "troika" of EU ministers visit Israel in the near future and they would hold talks with the PLO about whether it should be at Orient House, the PLO offices in East Jerusalem.

His statement appeared to back away from a possible showdown with the Israeli government, which has voiced strong opposition to any plan by the troika to visit the PLO in Jerusalem, which it sees as the unified capital of Israel.
Earlier Spring said the EU had decided on July 15 to visit the PLO in Orient House and would go ahead with the plan to show a balanced approach to Israel and the PLO.
But Irish officials said they were seeking clarification from the PLO itself as to whether or not it expected Orient House to be the venue of the troika talks.
Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy told Spring on Thursday his government would frown on such a plan, which would be seen as endorsement of the PLO's claims on Jerusalem as its capital.
Levy said PLO Chairman Yasser Arafat had agreed that the PLO would move its offices from Orient House to areas under PLO control and Sping said the EU would seek to clarify this.
"It is our intentions to have talks with the PLO," said Spring. "What is important is that we have a troika visit."

Earlier Spring said the three ministers, from Ireland, the Netherlands and Italy, were determined to visit the PLO in East Jerusalem but other EU ministers said the PLO itself might not want to anger the Netanyahu government.

"Maybe the symbolic importance of Orient House has declined," German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel told reporters. "Maybe it would be in the best interests of Palestinians to deal with Orient House differently," he said.

Spring called on Netanyahu's government to revive Middle East peace hopes and to withdraw from the city of Hebron as stipulated in the peace accords and allow free movement of people from Gaza and the West Bank.
He also urged the resumption of suspended talks between Israel and the Syrian government.
No date for the troika visit has been planned but ministers hoped it might take place before the year's end to review a peace process they fear might be slowed by Netanyahu's election.
Spring outraged the Israeli government last year by visiting Orient House. The Israeli president abruptly cancelled planned talks with Spring in retaliation.
The city's fate is supposed to be negotiated as part of the Middle East peace process. The new Israeli government insists, however, that it is the unified capital of Israel and will remain as such.
